method: EOS/BIP evaluation v5 (re-evaluated Nov 2026): the reference value is a local interpolation (ln x = a + b/T + c·ln(P−Psat) [+ d·ln²]) when the case is bracketed by measurements, otherwise a Krichevsky–Kasarnovsky physical extrapolation (ln(f₂/x) = A + B/T + V∞(P−Psat)/RT, validated by lowest-pressure leave-out). Each EOS has its BIP regressed on the band sample (≤30 points, 3:1 train/validation; thermopack 9 models: single kij/eps_kij; in-house Aspen variants: PR-BM·RKS-BM single kij, RK-ASPEN kaij+kbij, SR-POLAR kij+lij) and is ranked by the case x-AARD. The in-house implementations reproduce thermopack PR/SRK bubble pressures within 1e-4 in classic-α mode (polar α parameters set to 0 — no NH3 vapour-pressure gain with thermopack critical constants). v5.1: 1-parameter regressions stabilised (grid scan + validation-selected candidate; bubble-branch guard near the critical region); rows that cannot compute every case are flagged and ranked after full-coverage rows

source.provenance: Aspen Plus V14 TDE (NIST) literature binary VLE — Wiebe & Tremearne 1934 (273–373 K, 50–810 bar), Reamer & Sage 1959 (278–394 K, ≤414 bar, TPXY), Heise 1972 (239–294 K, 145–191 bar), a 4-point 298 K set. BVLE016 (211–295 K, 7.6–21.8 bar) was excluded: its implied Henry constant is about 10× lower than Wiebe/Reamer (inconsistent basis)
